title: AI Unlocked: Agriculture & Agribusiness
blurb: For farmers, cooperatives, and agripreneurs: advisory and diagnostic tools in the field, market and price intelligence, farm-business automation, precision-ag realities by budget level, and climate-smart planning — built for African and global contexts alike.

modules.t: AI on the Farm: The Real Map
modules.d: From smallholder advisory to precision agriculture — what works at each budget.
modules.body:
Three tiers of reality

  • Phone-only (smallholder): crop-disease photo diagnosis, advisory chatbots, market prices by SMS/WhatsApp — transformative and nearly free.
  • SME farm: record-keeping AI, drone imagery services, irrigation scheduling from weather data.
  • Industrial: satellite analytics, variable-rate application, yield prediction platforms.

This course teaches all three, weighted toward what pays back fastest at YOUR scale.

The FAO — the UN’s food and agriculture agency — frames digital and AI innovation as central to "transforming agrifood systems" for a planet of 10 billion. The frontier of that transformation is not the industrial mega-farm; it is the smallholder with a smartphone — which is exactly where this course begins.

modules.d: Photo-based crop health, livestock advisory, and extension at scale.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Photo diagnosis: leaf/pest images → probable causes → treatment options — verified against local extension guidance.
  • Advisory prompting: "Act as an agronomist for [crop] in [region/season]; my symptoms/inputs are…; give ranked actions with costs."
  • Extension multiplication: one agronomist's knowledge → localized voice notes, posters, and SMS tips for hundreds of farmers (the Public Health comms playbook, ruralized).
plAIbox™: run a two-week diagnosis-and-advisory pilot on one real crop cycle or livestock issue; log accuracy against expert confirmation.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

You are an agronomist-advisor for [crop/livestock] in [region, season]. My situation: [inputs, symptoms, budget]. Give ranked recommendations with local costs, what to verify with my extension officer before acting, a 30-day monitoring calendar, and the record-keeping template I should fill weekly by voice note.

modules.d: PlantVillage/Plantix-class apps, FAO/CGIAR data tools, satellite platforms — access paths.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • Plantix / PlantVillage Nuru-class apps: free photo diagnosis on ordinary smartphones — the smallholder entry point.
  • Advisory chatbots (WhatsApp-based ag services, national e-extension): check your country's programs — many are free.
  • Market data (commodity price apps, exchange feeds): daily price intelligence for selling decisions.
  • Imagery (OneSoil-class free satellite tools → paid drone services): field-zone insights scaling with budget.
  • General LLMs: business planning, records, and translation across all tiers.

modules.d: Records, ROI per plot, buyers, and the cooperative advantage.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Voice-note record keeping → AI-structured farm logs → per-plot ROI (the entrepreneurship tracker, soil edition).
  • Buyer prospecting and offtake proposals drafted; WhatsApp Business catalog for farm-gate sales.
  • Cooperatives: pooled data → collective bargaining briefs, input-purchase optimization, and grant/subsidy proposals (borrowing the NGO proposal engine).

modules.d: Weather-informed decisions, insurance, and honest uncertainty.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Season planning against forecast scenarios; planting-window analysis with stated uncertainty.
  • Index-insurance literacy: what AI-priced products cover and don't.
  • Risk registers for the farm: pests, price, weather, and mitigation actions — reviewed quarterly.

modules.d: A season plan with tools, costs, and expected ROI.
modules.body:
Capstone

  • One full-season AI-assisted plan: diagnosis/advisory stack, records system, market strategy, and climate risk register — with costs and projected ROI, presented to the panel.
